intro: The Auld Grey Town: a market town of limestone yards, mint cake and arts, at the gateway to the Lake District.
areas: Highgate, Stricklandgate and the old yards.
The River Kent and Abbot Hall.
Kendal Castle ruins above the town.
sights: Georgian house and gallery by the river.
Ruins with views over the town.
Elizabethan house with topiary gardens nearby.
eat: The famous energy bar taken up Everest.
arrive: Oxenholme Lake District station, just outside Kendal, is on the West Coast Main Line; a branch line serves Kendal and Windermere. Manchester Airport is about 90 minutes away.
around: Walkable town; Stagecoach buses run to Windermere and the Lakes.
pass: Stagecoach day tickets and Lakes passes; check current fares.
when: May–September for the Lakes; November for the Mountain Festival.
tip: Stay in Kendal for value and take the train to Windermere.

intro: Britain’s classic seaside resort: the Tower, the Illuminations, three piers and the Pleasure Beach.
areas: Blackpool Tower, the Golden Mile and Central Pier.
sights: Tower Eye, the Tower Ballroom and the Tower Circus.
Historic amusement park with record-breaking rollercoasters.
Miles of seafront lights each autumn.
eat: Sweet sticks of rock from seafront shops.
arrive: Blackpool North has trains to Manchester, Preston and London (via Preston). Manchester Airport is about 75 minutes away.
around: Heritage and modern trams run along the promenade; Blackpool Transport buses.
pass: Blackpool Transport day tickets cover trams and buses; check current fares.
when: Late August to early November for the Illuminations; summer for the beach.
tip: Ride the promenade tram after dark during the Illuminations.

intro: A Lancashire mill town with a grand town hall, a big market and moorland walks on its doorstep.
areas: Victoria Square and the Town Hall.
Rivington Pike and Winter Hill nearby.
sights: Tudor house where the spinning mule was invented.
Hilltop tower and terraced gardens nearby.
arrive: Bolton station has trains to Manchester (about 20 minutes) and Preston. Manchester Airport is about 30–40 minutes by train.
around: Bee Network buses and trains; the centre is walkable.
pass: Bee Network tickets and contactless capping; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn for the moors.
tip: Climb Rivington Pike for views over Lancashire.

intro: A Lancashire town known for its pier, rugby league, pies and canal-side heritage.
areas: Market Place and the Grand Arcade.
Canal-side heritage on the Leeds and Liverpool Canal.
sights: Canal wharf made famous by George Orwell.
Country park with trails and a hall.
Home of Wigan Warriors and Wigan Athletic (formerly the DW Stadium).
eat: Wigan is famous for its meat pies, even pie-eating contests.
night: Arts venue for gigs and comedy.
arrive: Wigan North Western (West Coast Main Line) and Wigan Wallgate stations. Manchester and Liverpool airports are under an hour away.
around: Bee Network buses and local trains.
pass: Bee Network tickets and contactless capping; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn; rugby league season (February–October).
tip: Catch a Warriors game for a real taste of the town.

intro: A Cheshire town between Manchester and Liverpool, with a gilded town hall gate and easy links across the North West.
areas: Golden Square, Time Square and Bridge Street.
Park with the Town Hall and Golden Gates.
sights: Georgian hall with ornate iron gates.
One of England’s oldest public museums.
arrive: Warrington Bank Quay (West Coast Main Line) and Warrington Central stations. Manchester and Liverpool airports are about 30 minutes away.
around: Warrington’s Own Buses serve the town.
pass: Warrington’s Own Buses day tickets; check current fares.
tip: Warrington is a handy base for both Manchester and Liverpool.

intro: A historic market town with a huge railway viaduct, hat-making heritage and a revived Underbanks.
areas: Historic market, independent shops and bars.
sights: One of Britain’s largest brick structures.
The UK’s only museum of hatting.
Underground tunnels from the Second World War.
eat: Brewery visitor centre in the town.
night: Restored Art Deco cinema and theatre.
arrive: Stockport station has fast trains to London Euston and Manchester (under 10 minutes). Manchester Airport is about 15 minutes away.
pass: Bee Network tickets and contactless capping; check current fares.
when: Year-round; spring to autumn for the Peak District nearby.
tip: Book an air raid shelter tour for a different side of the town.

intro: Scotland’s Granite City: silver-grey streets, a sandy beach, a historic fishing village and castle country nearby.
areas: St Machar’s Cathedral and King’s College.
Fishing village cottages and the long sandy beach.
sights: One of the world’s largest granite buildings.
night: Concerts in the restored Music Hall and at the P&J Live arena.
arrive: Aberdeen Airport is linked by bus to the city. Aberdeen station has trains to Edinburgh, Glasgow and London. NorthLink ferries sail to Orkney and Shetland.
around: First Aberdeen buses; the centre is walkable.
pass: First day tickets; check current fares.
when: May–September for long days and castles.
tip: Drive or take a bus to Dunnottar Castle on its clifftop.

intro: A waterfront city of design and discovery, home to V&A Dundee and Captain Scott’s ship.
areas: Seaside suburb with a castle and pubs.
night: Grand concert hall on City Square.
arrive: Dundee Airport has limited flights; Edinburgh is about an hour away. Dundee station has trains to Edinburgh, Glasgow and Aberdeen.
around: Xplore Dundee buses; walk the waterfront.
pass: Xplore Dundee day tickets; check current fares.
tip: Climb Dundee Law at sunset for views over the Tay bridges.

intro: Scotland’s historic heart: a royal castle on a crag, the Wallace Monument and two famous battlefields.
areas: Castle Wynd, the Church of the Holy Rude and cobbled streets.
sights: Tower with views over the battle sites.
night: Music venue in the Old Town.
Film and theatre at the university.
arrive: Stirling station has trains to Edinburgh and Glasgow (under an hour). Edinburgh and Glasgow airports are about 45 minutes away.
pass: First day tickets; check current fares.
tip: Buy castle tickets online in summer.

intro: The capital of the Highlands, on the River Ness, with Loch Ness and the North Coast 500 on its doorstep.
areas: Victorian Market, Eastgate and the castle.
The 1746 battlefield, east of the city.
sights: Cruises and Urquhart Castle on its shore.
Red sandstone castle on the river.
arrive: Inverness Airport is linked by bus. Inverness station has trains to Edinburgh, Glasgow and the Caledonian Sleeper to London.
around: Stagecoach buses; tours run to Loch Ness and Skye.
pass: Stagecoach day tickets; check current fares.
when: May–September for long days; midges are common in summer.
tip: Pack insect repellent and book Loch Ness cruises ahead in summer.

intro: Wales’s second city, on a sweeping bay, with the Mumbles and the Gower peninsula close by.
areas: Seaside village with a pier and ice cream.
sights: Britain’s first Area of Outstanding Natural Beauty, with Rhossili Bay.
eat: Wales’s largest indoor market, with cockles and laverbread.
night: Victorian theatre with touring shows and pantomime.
arrive: Swansea station has trains to London Paddington and Cardiff. Cardiff Airport is about an hour away.
around: First Cymru buses; the bay is great by bike.
pass: First day tickets; check current fares.
tip: Cycle the bay path from the city to Mumbles.

intro: A Welsh city on the River Usk with a rare transporter bridge, Roman Caerleon and a canal.
areas: Friars Walk, the Market and the riverfront.
sights: One of the few working transporter bridges in the world (check opening times).
Canal flight on the Monmouthshire and Brecon Canal.
eat: Restored indoor market with food stalls.
arrive: Newport station has trains to London Paddington, Cardiff and Bristol. Cardiff and Bristol airports are about 40 minutes away.
pass: Newport Bus day tickets; check current fares.
tip: Combine Caerleon’s Roman amphitheatre and barracks in one free visit.

sources.title: Museum Wales: National Roman Legion Museum

intro: A walled city with deep history and a creative spirit, on the River Foyle near the Donegal coast.
areas: Footbridge and square across the Foyle.
The murals and Free Derry Corner.
sights: Footbridge linking both banks of the Foyle.
Civil rights history in the Bogside.
The city’s story inside the walls.
night: One of Europe’s biggest Halloween celebrations.
arrive: City of Derry Airport is about 15 minutes away; Belfast airports are about 90 minutes. Derry~Londonderry station has trains to Belfast.
around: Walkable centre; Translink Foyle Metro buses.
pass: Translink day tickets; check current fares.
when: Spring to autumn; Halloween (late October) is huge.
tip: Walk the full circuit of the walls, about a mile.

intro: Ireland’s food capital, on an island in the River Lee, with a famous market and a creative, independent spirit.
areas: St Patrick’s Street and the English Market.
Church bells, cafés and the Butter Museum.
Harbour town and Titanic’s last port of call.
sights: Ring the bells of St Anne’s Church.
Kiss the Blarney Stone, just outside the city.
Fortress island and the Titanic Experience.
night: Guinness Cork Jazz Festival in late October.
arrive: Cork Airport is linked by bus. Kent station has trains to Dublin and Cobh. Brittany Ferries sail from Ringaskiddy.
around: Walkable centre; Bus Éireann city buses.
pass: Leap Card for cheaper bus fares; check current options.
when: May–September; the Jazz Festival in October.
tip: Visit the English Market early on a weekday.

intro: Ireland’s bohemian west-coast city of buskers, festivals and seafood, the gateway to Connemara.
areas: Shop Street, Quay Street and the Spanish Arch.
Pubs and restaurants on Dominick Street.
sights: Historic quays and the home of the Claddagh ring.
Grand domed cathedral by the river.
eat: Saturday market by St Nicholas’ Church.
night: Galway International Arts Festival (July) and Galway Races.
arrive: Shannon and Dublin airports are about 1–2.5 hours away by bus. Galway Ceannt station has trains to Dublin.
around: Walkable centre; city buses and tours to Connemara.
pass: Leap Card for city buses; check current options.
when: May–September; July for the Arts Festival and Races.
tip: Book Aran Islands ferries in advance in summer.

intro: A riverside city on the Shannon, with King John’s Castle, a lively market and rugby passion.
areas: King John’s Castle and St Mary’s Cathedral.
Elegant streets and the People’s Park.
The Shannon and the Hunt Museum.
sights: Art and antiquities in the Custom House.
night: Concerts and shows at the University of Limerick.
arrive: Shannon Airport is about 25 minutes away by bus. Limerick Colbert station has trains to Dublin.
around: Walkable centre; Bus Éireann city buses.
pass: Leap Card for city buses; check current options.
tip: Use Limerick as a base for the Cliffs of Moher.
